facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Brasilotitan nemophagus.
facts.quote: The type species is Brasilotitan nemophagus.

facts.statement: William R. Nava collected a partial sauropod skeleton in 2000 near Presidente Prudente in São Paulo state.
facts.quote: In 2000, William R. Nava collected the partial skeleton of a sauropod along a road in São Paulo state near Presidente Prudente city.

facts.statement: Elaine B. Machado and colleagues described the remains as the new species Brasilotitan nemophagus in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2013, a team of researchers, including Nava and led by Elaine B. Machado, described the remains as a new genus and species of sauropod, Brasilotitan nemophagus.

facts.statement: The genus name references Brazil and Greek Titans, while the species name combines Greek words for pasture and eat to reflect its herbivorous diet.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to its discovery in Brazil and to the Titans of Greek mythology, and the species epithet combines the Greek words némos "pasture, wood" and phagos "to eat", in reference to its herbivorous diet.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPM 125R is a partial skeleton including a dentary, cervical and sacral vertebrae, pelvic fragments, and an ungual phalanx.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MPM 125R, is a partial skeleton that consists of the right dentary, two partial cervical vertebrae, a partial sacrum, two fragments of the pelvis pertaining to the ilium and ischium, and an ungual phalanx.

facts.statement: Evidence of puncture marks and nearby theropod teeth suggests the holotype skeleton was scavenged by theropods before burial.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was likely scavenged by theropods before being buried, as some of the bones show puncture marks and theropod teeth were found alongside the skeleton.

facts.statement: Brasilotitan was a small sauropod, estimated to be less than 12 meters long.
facts.quote: Brasilotitan was small for a sauropod, probably less than 12 m long.

facts.statement: Brasilotitan possessed an L-shaped mandible that produced a squared-off snout, a feature shared with other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: As in several other titanosaurs, the mandible is L-shaped, producting a squared-off snout.

facts.statement: The symphyseal region of the dentary in Brasilotitan is slightly twisted medially, a feature never previously recorded in any titanosaur.
facts.quote: The symphyseal region of the dentary is slightly twisted medially, a feature never recorded before in any titanosaur.

facts.statement: The neural spines of the cervical vertebrae in Brasilotitan are relatively low.
facts.quote: The neural spines of the cervical vertebrae are relatively low.

facts.statement: Based on lower jaw morphology, Brasilotitan appears to be closely related to Antarctosaurus and Bonitasaura.
facts.quote: Based on lower jaw morphology, it appears to be closely related to Antarctosaurus and Bonitasaura.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses identify Brasilotitan as the sister taxon of the Brazilian titanosaur Uberabatitan.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses have found Brasilotitan to be the sister taxon of another Brazilian titanosaur, Uberabatitan.

facts.statement: Filippi et al. classified Brasilotitan within "Clade A", a group of titanosaurs characterized by square jaws.
facts.quote: Filippi et al. included Brasilotitan in what they called "Clade A", a grouping of titanosaurs with square jaws.

facts.statement: Brasilotitan lived during the Late Cretaceous (early Maastrichtian) in the Adamantina Formation of Brazil.
facts.quote: Brasilotitan (meaning "Brazil giant") is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (early Maastrichtian) Adamantina Formation of Brazil.

facts.statement: Brasilotitan nemophagus lived approximately between 94 and 84 million years ago during the Turonian and Santonian stages in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Brasilotitan nemophagus ("titán del Brasil comedor de plantas ") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Brasilotitan de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriano que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 94 y 84 millones de años, durante el Turoniense y el Santoniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Brasilotitan is estimated from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2017, Brusatte and colleagues suggested that some sauropod fossils attributed to the Adamantina Formation may actually originate from the Presidente Prudente Formation.
facts.quote: although in 2017 Brusatte and colleagues suggested that some of the sauropod fossils reported from the Adamantina Formation may actually come from the Presidente Prudente Formation.
